title: Features
description: Machine-checkable ground truth for plan completion. Inviolable — agents may only flip passes false->true with evidence_refs.

steps.description: Verification steps the verifier must perform end-to-end

acceptance.description: Machine-checkable condition — the exact test for passes=true

tier_override.description: Force different audit tier for this feature only

allOf.description: If passes=true, evidence_refs and verified_by required

proof.description: Optional cheap first-principle proof this feature carries on its own: the measurement that would show the feature delivers, and how it is taken. Same shape as objective_contract.schema.json's delivers[].proof — the two are kept in lockstep. A feature that carries one is scored as a slice in its own right by the lock/close scorer (plan 2026-08-13-001 F002), so a plan whose features each carry a proof needs no delivers[] to state an outcome. Optional by design: absence means the feature is not a slice, not that it is invalid.

metric.description: The cheap measurement that would show this feature delivers — a threshold, a count, an observable state change. Substantive enough that a reader can tell whether it was met (hence the 10-character floor); not a KPI programme.

method.description: How the metric is taken. 'walk' — a human or agent walks the path end-to-end. 'request' — a single call against a running surface. 'named_test' — an existing or new test identified by name. 'probe' — a one-off script or query run against real state. Closed set on purpose, identical to delivers[].proof.method.

surface.description: Optional — where the proof is taken. Mirrors the plan-level `surfaces` enum in plan.schema.json.

user_impact.description: Optional declared user impact — who feels this feature and how. Consumed by the decision brief rendered at human approval gates. Optional by design (D003): a feature that declares nothing renders 'user impact not declared' rather than a synthesized claim.

audience.description: Who experiences the change. 'none' means genuinely internal work with no external consequence, and is a complete declaration on its own.

summary.description: One plain-language line naming what the audience experiences differently. Required (>=10 chars) unless audience is 'none'.

surfaces.description: Where the impact lands. Mirrors the plan-level `surfaces` enum in plan.schema.json — the two are kept in lockstep and asserted identical by scripts/test_user_impact_contract.py. Required (non-empty) unless audience is 'none'.

description_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the UTF-8 encoded feature `description` this declaration was written against. Staleness anchor per D005: a mismatch marks the brief possibly-stale rather than presenting an old claim as current. Required whenever the declaration carries a claim (audience other than 'none') so the consuming brief in F003 never has to invent a fourth 'digest unknown' state alongside declared / possibly-stale / undeclared. Optional under audience 'none', which asserts no external consequence and so has no claim that can go stale.

then.description: D003: 'none' is the entire declaration — summary and surfaces must be absent or empty.

else.description: Any audience other than 'none' owes a real summary, at least one surface, and the digest that binds the claim to the description it was written against.

uri.description: Relative path, git SHA, or Firebase Storage signed URL

captured_by.description: Agent or tool that captured the evidence
